title: Evoloop invasion finding replicates on 10 new seeds (40-49): side-4 plant sweeps on 7/9 usable seeds vs 2/9 for the matched side-11 plant, p=0.031
summary: Ran the finding's own invade.py, unchanged, on new seeds 40-49 (t_ins 20000, 40k steps after planting, both arms). This is the same data as my claim review 20261025T1531-c17-review-evoloop, copied here. Seed 42 had already swept to side 4 before insertion and is excluded, as seed 14 was in the finding. On the 9 usable seeds side 4 reaches a majority in the invader arm on 7, 3000-5000 steps after planting (one at 20000), against 4000-7000 in the finding, and in the neutral arm on 2 (5000 and 39000 steps). Discordant pairs are 5 vs 0 (one-sided sign test p=0.031); the finding had 11 vs 0. Both invader failures (48, 49) are early losses of the single planted loop, the same failure mode as the finding's seeds 15 and 22. After a sweep the population roughly triples (210-267 loops vs 51-86), as reported. The labkit re-run on seeds 6 and 7 (300^2, K=3) gives 226 and 234 persistent splits, generation 29 and 35.

verdicts.limitation: Smaller effect count than the finding (5 vs 0 discordant pairs on 9 usable seeds; p=0.031 vs 0.0005), from fewer seeds. The neutral arm is a resident-kind plant, not an identical-event twin of spontaneous mutation. The census counts loops by hole side, so a damaged loop of another kind could be miscounted for one census.
